questions.question: In India, _________ was the final approval authority for the five year plans.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**National Development Council.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Development Council (NDC)** was the** final approval authority **for the five year plans in India.
 
• The NDC was established in **August 1952 **as a **non-statutory body **to facilitate coordination between the** Centre and the States **on matters of **national development.**
 
• **The Prime Minister of India** was the** ex-officio chairman **of the NDC, and the members included **Cabinet Ministers, Chief Ministers of States, and experts** from various fields.
 
• The NDC played a crucial role in** formulating and implementing **the** five year plans**, which aimed at achieving **rapid economic growth, social justice, and self-reliance.**
 
• The International Development Council, National Agriculture and Development Council, and National Development Centre are **not valid options** as they are not relevant to the context and **do not exist** in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• The **five year plans** were a series of **national development plans** that were initiated by the** Indian government** after independence in **1947.**
 
• The **first five year plan** was launched in** 1951**, and a total of **12 plans** were implemented until **2017.**
 
• The five year plans focused on various sectors such as **agriculture, industry, infrastructure, education, health, and social welfare.**
 
• The five year plans were based on the principles of **democratic socialism**, which emphasized the role of the state in **promoting economic growth** and **social welfare.**
 
• Hence, the statement "The National Development Council was the final approval authority for the five year plans in India" is **correct.**

questions.question: Which of the following monetary instruments of RBI is qualitative in nature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Moral Suasion.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Moral suasion** is a** qualitative monetary instrument** used by the **RBI **to **persuade banks** to act in a certain way without actually mandating them to do so.
 
• It involves using **informal communication** and** persuasion techniques** to influence the** behavior of banks **and other financial institutions.
 
• This instrument is used to maintain** financial stability, regulate credit flow, and ensure compliance **with monetary policy objectives.
 
• **Cash reserve ratio, bank rate, and open market operations **are all quantitative monetary instruments that involve **controlling the supply of money** in the economy through** direct interventions** in the money market.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cash reserve ratio** is the percentage of **deposits** that banks are required to keep with the **RBI **as a reserve.
 
• **Bank rate **is the** interest rate** at which the RBI lends to **commercial banks.**
 
• **Open market operations** involve **buying and selling government securities **to control the money supply.
 
• Hence, the** correct answer **is option 1 - Moral suasion.

questions.question: What is the phenomenon of heavy showers with thunder occurring in the West Bengal region during the hot weather season called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kalbaisakhi.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phenomenon of** heavy showers** with** thunder **occurring in the **West Bengal region** during the** hot weather **season is called **Kalbaisakhi.**
 
• Kalbaisakhi is a local term derived from** two Bengali words: Kal** (time) and **Baisakhi **(the first month of the Bengali calendar).
 
• These showers are accompanied by **strong winds, lightning, and hailstorms, **and can cause **damage to crops, houses, and electric poles.**
 
• Kalbaisakhi typically occurs between **April and June**, and is caused by the** collision of hot and humid air **from the** Bay of Bengal **with** cooler air** from the** Himalayas.****​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Loo **is a term used in **North India** for** hot and dry winds** that blow during the **summer season**, and can cause **dehydration and heat strokes.**
 
• **Retreating monsoon** refers to the **withdrawal of the southwest monsoon** from the Indian subcontinent, which usually begins in **September **and ends in **October.**
 
• **Mango showers**, also known as **pre-monsoon showers**, are a phenomenon that occurs in the** southern and western parts** of India in the months of** April and May, **and are named so because they coincide with the **flowering of mango trees.**

questions.question: Only the ________ can make the proclamation of emergency in India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **proclamation of emergency in India** can only be made by the** President of India,** who is the **head of state** and the** commander-in-chief **of the **armed forces.**
 
• The **Constitution of India** provides for** three types** of emergencies:** national** emergency, **state **emergency, and** financial **emergency.
 
• In case of a **national emergency, **the** President** can declare emergency on the grounds of** war, external aggression, or armed rebellion**.
 
• The decision to impose emergency must be approved by the **Union Cabinet** and ratified by **both houses of Parliament.**
 
• The **Governor of a state** can declare **state emergency** in case of **failure of constitutional machinery **in the state, but only on the advice of the **Council of Ministers** headed by the **Chief Minister.**
 
• The **Chief Minister** is the head of the **Council of Ministers** in a state and is responsible for the **administration of the state.**
 
• However, the Chief Minister does not have the** power to proclaim emergency **in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Governor of a state** is appointed by the** President **and is the** constitutional head of the state,** but acts on the **advice of the Council of Ministers **headed by the **Chief Minister**.
 
• The **Chief Minister **is appointed by the** Governor **and is the leader of the** ruling party or coalition **in the state legislature.
 
 
• The Chief Minister is responsible for the** day-to-day administration** of the state and for** implementing the policies **of the state government.
 
 
 
• The **Prime Minister** is the head of the **Union Council of Ministers** and is responsible for the** overall administration** of the country.
 
 
• However, the Prime Minister** does not have** the power to** proclaim emergency **in India.
 
 
 
• The **President of India** is elected by an** electoral college **consisting of the **elected members **of both **houses of Parliament **and the **elected members of the Legislative Assemblies **of the states.
 
 
• The President is the** head of state** and represents the **unity of the nation.**

questions.question: What do you call organisms made of more than one cell?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**multicellular.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Multicellular organisms** are made up of **more than one cell** and are **complex** in structure compared to **unicellular organisms.**
 
• Multicellular organisms have **specialized cells** that perform **specific functions** and work together to maintain the** organism's survival.**
 
• Examples of multicellular organisms include **plants, animals, and fungi.**
 
• **Subcellular **refers to structures or processes that occur within a **single cell**, while **paracellular** refers to the** movement of substances** between cells.
 
• **Unicellular organisms** are made up of a** single cell **and can carry out all necessary functions for survival within that cell.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subcellular:** Examples of subcellular structures include organelles such as the **nucleus, mitochondria, and ribosomes.**
 
• **Paracellular:** This movement can occur through gaps between **adjacent cells or through specialized protein **channels that span the cell membrane.
 
• **Unicellular:** Examples of unicellular organisms include **bacteria and protists.**

questions.question: ________ is a process in which two close-fitting parts are joined by using a filler material which is heated above its melting point and distributed in the gap by capillary action.
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Brazing** is the process in which** two close-fitting parts** are joined by using a **filler material** which is **heated above its melting point **and distributed in the gap by capillary action.
 
• **Hardening:** This option is** incorrect **as it does not involve joining two parts using a filler material.
 
• **Soldering:** This option is** incorrect **as it involves joining two parts using a filler material but the filler material is not heated above its melting point.
 
• **Welding: **This option is **incorrect **as it involves joining two parts by melting the surfaces of the parts and not by using a filler material.
 
• Therefore, the **correct** answer is option 4, Brazing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hardening:** It is a process of making a **metal harder** by** heating it** and then **cooling it rapidly.**
 
• **Soldering:** It is a process in which two or more metal items are** joined **together by** melting and flowing a filler metal **into the joint.
 
• **Welding:** It is a process of** joining two or more metal parts** by heating the surfaces to their **melting point **and joining them together.

• 'Make in India' is a** flagship programme** launched by the** Government of India** in **September 2014 **to encourage** domestic and foreign companies** to manufacture their products in India.
 
• The programme aims to **boost the manufacturing sector **and create **job opportunities** in India. 
 
• In the last 8 years, the programme has attracted **significant investments** in various sectors such as **automobiles, electronics, defence, and pharmaceuticals.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 -** '5 years' is** incorrect** as it refers to the completion of the programme in 2019.
 
• **Option 2** - '9 years' and **option 3** - '4 years' are also** incorrect** as they do not match with the timeline of the programme.
 
• Hence, the **correct **answer is option 4 - '8 years'.

questions.question: Items such as cars, clothes, chocolates, which are directly sold to the consumers are :
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**private goods.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Private goods** are those goods that are **directly sold **to the consumers and are **exclusive** in nature.
 
• These goods are owned by **individuals** and **not shared** by the public.
 
• **Cars, clothes, and chocolates** are examples of **private goods** as they are sold to the consumers **directly** and are** owned by individuals.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Expensive goods** are **not a correct **option as the price of the goods** does not determine** whether they are private or public goods.
 
• **Public goods** are those goods that are available for** use by the public, **and their consumption by one individual does not reduce their availability for others.
 
 
• Examples of public goods include** parks, streetlights, and public libraries.**
 
 
 
• **Capital goods** are goods that are used in the **production of other goods and services**, such as machinery, equipment, and factories.
 
• Therefore, the **correct** answer to the question is option 1, private goods.
